correctness.rationale: For generic projected half-lengths X>Y>Z, a section crosses 3,4,5 edges after passing the first 1,2,3 vertices: the induced cube-graph prefix has 0,1,2 internal edges, respectively. At the fourth vertex the prefix is a star if X<Y+Z (giving 6 crossings), and a square otherwise (giving 4); reflection supplies the upper half of the sweep. The signed-height gaps therefore give the stated offset lengths for independent generators, orthogonal or not. The angular normalization is E[2s]=a+b+c, not uniform directions among hit planes. The spherical divergence identity has the stated sign and factor 1/2 with inward co-normals. In the minimum partition the coordinate-edge contribution sums to (π/2)A, and each shared equality edge contributes minus its length times the appropriate pair norm. In the defect partition the boundary of the triangle inequalities contributes Lβ_i, and equality edges contribute minus their pair norms twice; the arcs from q to its normalized coordinate-plane projections have length arcsin q_k. These checks give both moments and the cube specialization. A separate face-intersection offset calculation passed the identity on 216 integer directions for a skew parallelotope and a 100×100 equal-area midpoint quadrature agreed to within 8.5×10⁻⁵ in the cube and two unequal boxes. Replay: python3 /workspace/reproductions/frozen_checks.py 5; bounded quadrature corroborates the proof, not its continuum quantifiers.
